To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose an algorithm to mine extraction rules from training data, and we show that training neural models with both human annotated data and data automatically labeled by these mined rules can significantly improve performance.
we can improve neural models with mined rules as weak supervision, and that the combination of human and rule labeled data can improve performance.

(1) we propose a rule mining algorithm to automatically label a large amount aspect and opinion term data; (2) we show that neural models trained on the combination of human labeled data and rule labeled data can achieve performance better than and comparable with the current best performance; (3) we provide a detailed discussion of the challenges and solutions in training neural models with rule labeled data
In summary, our research is concerned with
two aspects.
the neural aspect and opinion term (AOT) extraction task, which is to extract the aspect terms (ATs) and opinion terms (OTs) from sentences in a review.
how to make neural models more effective and efficient with weak supervision, which can be applied in many other tasks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed weakly supervised method can be used to improve neural models on aspect and opinion term identification.
we have developed a novel approach that combines neural networks with mined extraction rules to alleviate the data scarcity problem in aspect and opinion term detection.
the neural aspect and opinion term extractors can be trained with a large number of auxiliary data that is automatically labeled by the mined rules.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mined rules are weak supervision which can improve the neural aspect and opinion term extractor.

the proposed weak supervision approach can help neural models achieve performance comparable to the current best systems, while the neural model can help the weak supervision approach achieve better performance than the rule-based approach alone.

we can train an end-to-end neural model for aspect term and opinion term extraction by using a small amount of human annotated training data and a large amount of rule labeled data, which are automatically extracted from existing training data by our proposed rule mining algorithm.
The main takeaway from our work is that
neural models can benefit from weak supervision.
neural models can benefit a lot from the weakly supervised data labeled by simple and fast extraction rules.
the combination of human and weakly supervised data can be a promising approach for training neural models for NLP tasks.
